required_facts.statement: A Config managed rule evaluates supported resource configuration against the rule’s criteria and configured parameters.
Choose the supplied rule, resource scope and parameters, run or inspect its evaluation, and compare compliant and noncompliant sample resources.
Read each evaluation’s resource ID and compliance result rather than treating the presence of the rule as proof that all resources passed.

teaching_blocks.title: The situation
teaching_blocks.content: A managed Config rule is present, but the operator still needs to verify its scope, parameters and actual evaluation results. Rule existence is setup evidence, not the compliance result for every resource.

teaching_blocks.title: The operating model
teaching_blocks.content: A Config managed rule evaluates supported resource configuration against the rule’s criteria and configured parameters.

teaching_blocks.title: How the check works
teaching_blocks.content:
Choose the supplied rule, resource scope and parameters, run or inspect its evaluation, and compare compliant and noncompliant sample resources.

Read each evaluation’s resource ID and compliance result rather than treating the presence of the rule as proof that all resources passed.

teaching_blocks.title: Work through one sandbox case
teaching_blocks.content:
Choose the supplied rule and configure its approved resource scope and parameters. Run or inspect evaluation and compare the supplied compliant and noncompliant sample resources. For each sample, record the resource ID and compliance result, then relate that result to the rule criteria. If a noncompliant sample is still reported as compliant, inspect the chosen scope and parameters against the supplied requirement rather than accepting the presence of the rule as success. This example checks automated configuration evaluation; it does not install a remediation workflow or assume that a compliance report establishes malicious activity.

Use the two supplied sample results as a boundary check, not just a success example. One compliant result establishes that the intended acceptable configuration can pass; the noncompliant sample checks that the prohibited configuration is reported. If a sample is outside the configured scope, its result cannot validate the intended in-scope criterion. Tie each inspected resource ID to the configured rule scope and parameters.

teaching_blocks.title: Do not confuse the evidence
teaching_blocks.content: A configured rule does not mean all resources passed. Read individual evaluation resource IDs and compliance results. The rule evaluates supported configuration against its criteria and parameters; the actual results must be checked.

video_need.reason: Rule scope, parameters and individual compliant/noncompliant results benefit from one controlled configuration evaluation demonstration.

practice_anchor.objective: Run the supplied Config managed rule in a prepared sandbox using the approved resource scope and parameters, then inspect evaluations for the supplied compliant and noncompliant sample resources.
practice_anchor.success: The selected rule, scope and parameters match the supplied requirement. Each sample's resource ID and compliance result are recorded: the compliant sample passes and the noncompliant sample is flagged. Rule presence alone is not accepted as evidence of compliance, and no remediation is performed.

visual_anchor.purpose: Show the selected Config managed rule, its configured resource scope and parameters, and individual evaluation rows identifying the supplied compliant and noncompliant resources by resource ID and compliance result.

teaching_notes: Do not add remediation behavior to a detection-only rule task.

required_facts.statement: An AWS budget compares cost or usage with a configured budget amount over a selected period.
Create a cost budget with the approved scope, amount and period, then configure an actual or forecast threshold and approved notification recipient.
A notification alerts its recipients; stopping resources requires separately configured actions rather than the notification itself.

teaching_blocks.title: The situation
teaching_blocks.content: An approved cost threshold should alert a named recipient. Configure the budget scope and notification deliberately, and do not describe an alert as an automatic resource stop.

teaching_blocks.title: The operating model
teaching_blocks.content: An AWS budget compares cost or usage with a configured budget amount over a selected period.

teaching_blocks.title: How the check works
teaching_blocks.content:
Create a cost budget with the approved scope, amount and period, then configure an actual or forecast threshold and approved notification recipient.

A notification alerts its recipients; stopping resources requires separately configured actions rather than the notification itself.

teaching_blocks.title: Work through one sandbox case
teaching_blocks.content: Use the approved period, amount and scope for the cost budget. Choose the supplied actual or forecast threshold and approved notification recipient. Compare the configuration with those supplied inputs and retain the recipient setting. The budget compares cost or usage with an amount over a period; the notification alerts recipients. Any resource-stopping action would need separate configuration and is not part of this notification example.

teaching_blocks.title: Do not confuse the evidence
teaching_blocks.content: A budget notification does not itself stop resources. It alerts recipients; separately configured actions are required for stopping behavior. Do not imply that notification setup caps the workload's spending.

video_need.reason: A short budget-settings walkthrough helps locate period, scope and recipient settings; text suffices to distinguish alerts from actions.

practice_anchor.objective: Set one sandbox cost budget using the supplied approved scope, amount and period, with one actual or forecast threshold notification sent to the approved recipient.
practice_anchor.success: The saved budget matches the supplied scope, amount and period. Exactly one notification matches the supplied threshold value, actual or forecast basis, and approved recipient. No resource-stopping actions are configured.

visual_anchor.purpose: Show the configured sandbox cost budget's scope, amount and period alongside its single notification's threshold value, actual or forecast basis, and recipient.

teaching_notes: Use supplied amounts and thresholds; do not estimate workload cost or configure unrequested budget actions.
